steps.title: Два будущих — две разные задачи
steps.html:
They are going to move onto the water. — решение уже принято. Это видно заранее.

The first families will move in before the end of the decade. — прогноз о том, что будет.

I'll take my camera, too. — говорящий решает прямо сейчас, в момент речи.

steps.title: В каком предложении решение принято заранее?
options: I'm going to take an extra sweater — it's cold.
It's cold. I'll take a sweater, then.
The water will be quite calm.
steps.answer: I'm going to take an extra sweater — it's cold.
steps.why: Be going to сообщает о плане, который уже был.

steps.title: Какая форма и когда
steps.html:
ФормаКогда используемПример
be going toрешение уже принято; планThe government is going to develop artificial islands.
be going toпрогноз, для которого уже есть признакиLook at those clouds — it's going to rain.
willпрогноз, мнение о будущемThe first families will move in this decade.
willрешение в момент речи; предложение или обещаниеI'll take my camera, too.
present continuousдоговорённость с точным временем и местомWe're visiting the islands tomorrow.

steps.title: Как это работает
steps.html:
Разница в том, когда принято решение, а не когда произойдёт действие. Обе формы говорят об одном и том же будущем.

Для прогноза подходят обе. Going to — когда доказательство перед глазами: She's going to fall (она уже качается). Will — когда это ваше мнение: I think she'll be fine.

Для договорённости со временем, местом и другим человеком естественнее Present Continuous: We're meeting the guide at nine.

steps.title: Послушайте примеры.

I'm sure the water on the lake will be quite calm.
It's quite cold, so I'm going to take an extra sweater.
I believe we'll be able to ask them questions through a guide.
It would be great to have some photos, so I'll take my camera, too.

steps.title: Living on the water
steps.html:
Прочитайте один раз. Обратите внимание на формы будущего — их несколько.

Ask people where they would live if land ran out, and most of them will say the suburbs, or somewhere inland where a house is cheaper. A growing number are answering differently. They are going to move onto the water.

On Lake Titicaca, the Uros have done it for centuries. Their islands are built from reeds, tied together and replaced from the top as the bottom rots away. Nothing about the place is permanent, and that is the point: when a family needs more space, the inhabitants simply make room by adding another layer and another island. The children go to school by boat. Solar panels power the televisions.

In Amsterdam the same idea arrives with a mortgage. A district of floating houses sits on a canal north of the centre, each one moored to a steel post so that it rises and falls with the water. Buyers say they feel at home within a week. What they miss is not the ground; it is the shops. There is one communal building, a shared laundry, and a ferry that leaves every twenty minutes and is packed like sardines at half past eight.

The Maldives is planning something larger. As the sea rises, the government is going to develop artificial islands, and the first families will move in before the end of the decade. Critics point out that the project will cost more than the country earns in a year, and that nobody knows how the structures will behave in a serious storm.

None of this is a holiday. You have to check the ropes after a storm, you have to carry everything you buy, and you can't simply walk to a shop at eleven at night. But ask anyone who has settled down on the water whether they will move back, and the answer is almost always the same: not a chance.

steps.title: Послушайте дневник путешествия. Почему автор берёт лишний свитер?
options: Потому что холодно, хотя день солнечный
Потому что поездка на лодке долгая
steps.answer: Потому что холодно, хотя день солнечный
steps.html:
Прочитайте один раз. Обратите внимание на формы будущего — их несколько.

Ask people where they would live if land ran out, and most of them will say the suburbs, or somewhere inland where a house is cheaper. A growing number are answering differently. They are going to move onto the water.

On Lake Titicaca, the Uros have done it for centuries. Their islands are built from reeds, tied together and replaced from the top as the bottom rots away. Nothing about the place is permanent, and that is the point: when a family needs more space, the inhabitants simply make room by adding another layer and another island. The children go to school by boat. Solar panels power the televisions.

In Amsterdam the same idea arrives with a mortgage. A district of floating houses sits on a canal north of the centre, each one moored to a steel post so that it rises and falls with the water. Buyers say they feel at home within a week. What they miss is not the ground; it is the shops. There is one communal building, a shared laundry, and a ferry that leaves every twenty minutes and is packed like sardines at half past eight.

The Maldives is planning something larger. As the sea rises, the government is going to develop artificial islands, and the first families will move in before the end of the decade. Critics point out that the project will cost more than the country earns in a year, and that nobody knows how the structures will behave in a serious storm.

None of this is a holiday. You have to check the ropes after a storm, you have to carry everything you buy, and you can't simply walk to a shop at eleven at night. But ask anyone who has settled down on the water whether they will move back, and the answer is almost always the same: not a chance.

steps.title: Как говорить о том, что впереди

items.text: I'm going to… / I've decided to…

steps.title: Ответьте вслух.
items: Смогли бы вы жить на воде? Что было бы труднее всего?
Как изменится ваш город за двадцать лет? Дайте два прогноза.
Что вы собираетесь с этим делать — одно уже принятое решение.

steps.title: Теперь ответьте целиком одним высказыванием. Запишите себя.
steps.sub: Используйте will для прогнозов и going to для решений.
items: I don't think I could live … because …
In twenty years my city will … and it probably won't …
I'm going to … , and I'll … if I can.

steps.title: Урок 10 пройден
items: Я могу делать прогнозы о будущем.
Я выбираю между will, be going to и Present Continuous.
Я по-прежнему говорю, что люди обязаны и не обязаны делать.
Я могу описать место и его ландшафт.
